entries.text: Who is taking the new starter?
Do we have a board for the Lisbon launch? Ask me which one I mean with your clarify tool, offering 'Uffici task board' and 'Another app'. [ask-a-question]
Which office should I book a desk in? Ask me with your clarify tool, offering 'Lisbon' and 'Porto'. [ask-a-question]

Please remember for later, with your uffici_remember tool: invoices for the Lisbon client go out on the 10th. [remember-this]

steps.note: 🔴 `nonEmpty`, not `contains`, and the reason is a division of labour. What an end-to-end run proves is that the pieces CONNECT: a ring became a brief, a harness answered, a post came back over the wire. What a model SAYS is the one thing that legitimately varies — three shapes of a 'repeat this token' ask were tried against DeepSeek V4 Flash and it answered conversationally every time, which is the agent behaving well. Rendering is pinned deterministically where it belongs, in the plugin's own renderer tests, which assert exactly what text a brief becomes. 🔴 And `withinMs` is the ring's deadline, never less: until the platform expires the request an answer is on time, and a 60s window failed real-model posts landing at 64-66s (#2164, ledger class 22).

🔴 The gate, and the reason there is no `wait` before it. Onboarding was rung above while this turn was still running — that overlap is what the script is here to exercise — but the NEXT ring on invoices must not arrive until this turn has closed, or it supersedes it. A fixed wait cannot know: the mock answers in milliseconds and a real model took anywhere from 3s to 83s in one run, so both guesses that were tried (25s, then 62s) lost.

entries.text: Thanks. Anything else outstanding?

steps.note: Gate before the third invoices ring.

steps.note: Gate, and what makes the offset assertion below deterministic: an offset is only advanced by a close, so asserting it after a timed wait asserts how fast the harness is.
Every close so far answered, so the offset has walked to the cause.
Onboarding's first turn, gated before its second ring below.

entries.text: Never mind, ignore this one [say-nothing]

steps.note: The injected cancel's own close. Waiting for it rather than for a clock is what stops the run ending while the cancel is still in flight.

entries.text: And the desk booking? [answer-slowly]

steps.note: 🔴 The expiry this ring exists to demonstrate must close a request the plugin ACCEPTED, so the deadline must outlive the ack and still fall inside the turn. Both ends were machine-calibrated before: 1ms lost to the 100ms expiry sweep, and 500ms lost to the ack itself on a runner at load 24, which reported `resumed` one short (#2305, ledger class 22). So the turn is made long on purpose — `[answer-slowly]` holds it for the mock's 30s — and the deadline sits far from both: 10s is twenty times the 500ms an ack overran and 20s inside the turn. `uffici-compose-profile.test.mjs` pins that pairing.

The expiry's close — `error` (`timeout`, the plugin took the brief) since #2842: an expired request is never `cancelled`, which the platform keeps silent. The ring's `deadlineMs` above is the assertion; this waits for what it causes.
🔴 #2232: the agent ASKS. The model mock calls Hermes's clarify on the marker (a real model is asked to in words), and the plugin turns it into the question card.
🔴 `question`, never `nonEmpty`: a harness that fell back to plain text also posts, and the person would get a numbered list instead of the card.
🔴 The question SETTLES its request: the person sees the card, not a working line, and the deadline stops running against a turn that is waiting on them.

entries.text: Uffici task board

steps.note: The answer, as the card posts it. The plugin resolves the waiting clarify with it rather than starting a turn, and acknowledges `resumed`.
The turn that asked carries on and answers — on THIS request, the one that carried the answer.
The asking turn's end closes the answering request: without the continuation it would close nothing, and this request would expire.

🔴 #2235, a cancel mid-question. A question SETTLES its request, so the platform has nothing open to cancel; the one real path that cancels a turn blocked on a question is its question post failing upstream, which makes the companion withdraw the request that asked. The plugin must release the question before it stops the turn (#2233), or the turn keeps Hermes's session and the next ring waits behind it until its deadline.
The refused question: the companion closes the asking request as an error, which is what tells the person, and withdraws it from the plugin.

entries.text: Lisbon, please — go ahead and book it.

steps.note: The person's next message. The turn that asked must be over by now; if it still held the session, this ring would queue behind it and expire.
`contains` the mock's reply prefix, not `nonEmpty`: a turn that asked again would post the question, and that is not the answer this scenario is for.
🔴 #2235, a harness restart mid-turn. The marker holds the model's answer for 30s, so the turn is still running when the harness restarts.
The driver restarts the harness's container on the line this logs. The step holds until the NEW process has been handed the request again (#2234); a reconnect of the old one would get nothing.
The request the old process held, answered by the new one — never left to its deadline.

The agent's Uffici tools. The catalog is the AGENT's, served for every conversation — a plugin that registers one catalog for its whole harness process finds `list_boards` whichever conversation it listed first. The model mock calls `list_boards` on the marker when the catalog offers it; the plugin carries the call through the companion's `tools.call`, and the scripted result comes back.

The model mock calls `uffici_rerun` on the marker with the latest `tool_call` URN its session carries — the earlier `list_boards` result's — and the plugin carries it through the companion's `tools.rerun`; the scripted host finds the call in THIS conversation and answers the tool's result again.
The re-run reached the platform side, on THIS request — not merely offered.
`contains` the board's name, which only the re-run's result carries: this turn's own message never names it.

🔴 #2386, the agent's memory. The model mock calls `uffici_remember` on the marker (a real model is asked to in words) with a fact carrying the memory canary; the plugin carries it through the companion's `memory.remember`, and the scripted host keeps it on this conversation.
The fact reached the platform side, on THIS request.
Gate before the recall ring.

entries.text: When do the Lisbon invoices go out?

steps.note: 🔴 The recall. Before Hermes calls the model, the plugin's memory provider asks `memory.recall` with the turn's text; the fact shares its words, so it comes back and Hermes fences it into `<memory-context>` on the USER side. The runners judge that from the model mock's `memory_recalled` boolean — never its text. `onboarding`'s turns are the outage: the script takes memory down there, and each of them must tell the model so inside the same fence.
The prefetch reached the platform side on THIS request, before the answer.

🔴 #2414, a session the harness REPLACES. `withinMs` is the driver's whole window — it notices the line within a second, then a `docker exec` starts Python and ends the row — and is generous because a ring that beats the end is answered `resumed`, which reads as the very defect this step exists to catch. The driver ends this conversation's session inside the real Hermes — its row in `state.db`, which a live gateway reads when the next message routes, and then answers with a new session that has no history. A plugin that read its session index's key acked `resumed` here: no opener came, and the agent answered the newest message of a conversation it could not see. This step proves nothing by itself; the ring below does.

entries.text: Back to the Lisbon invoice — is it settled now?

steps.note: FRESH, on a conversation resumed three times before: the session it ran on is gone.
The conversation before the delta reaches the new session.

🔴 #2679, the first use case: a person's PDF and PNG. The companion prefetches both into the shared workspace (two downloads through the fixture's loopback files routes), the plugin hands them to Hermes as media — the PNG as an image part, the PDF as a document at a local path — and the mock names each canary only when it found it in the bytes it was given. The member's text names neither canary, so an echo cannot pass.

🔴 The interrupted transfer: the next upload's connection drops 64 KiB into its PATCH, once. The companion resumes from the offset a HEAD reports, the run passes, and the tally's `uploadsResumed` says it happened.

entries.text: Please make me the Q3 report as a PDF and attach it to your reply. [make-a-file]

steps.note: The second use case, attached: the mock writes the report INSIDE the shared workspace and answers `MEDIA:<path>`; Hermes delivers it through the adapter's send_document, the plugin uploads it with files.upload, and a post carries it.
Exactly one attachment, and it is an upload of this request that arrived with the CRC32C its grant was minted for — what the person downloads is what the harness wrote.

entries.text: Now save that report into Files at reports/q3-report.pdf with your uffici_upload tool. [save-a-file]

steps.note: The second use case, saved: uffici_upload with `to`, the file at the place the agent chose.

assert.note:
🔴 The closes and sessions ARE asserted here, as a tally. An earlier version of this block carried a note saying so while listing neither, so every close outcome was unasserted — the note described a property the file did not have.

A tally rather than positional `expectClose` steps because a real harness finishes turns at times a script cannot predict: a cancel races a fast reply, an expiry's deadline passes mid-flight, and an ordered expectation then matches whichever request happens to be current and fails for a reason about scheduling.

🔴 No `empty` close appears, and that is a measured absence rather than an oversight. The empty-turn ring asks the model to say nothing through a marker in its text, and the model mock honours that — proven directly in `tests/test_model_mock.py`. It does not survive the journey: Hermes builds its own prompt rather than passing an entry's text through, so the marker never reaches the model and the turn answers. `empty` is therefore demonstrated at the unit level and NOT end to end, and this file says so instead of asserting a count that only sometimes holds.

🔴 `posts` IS asserted (#2273): a harness restart mid-turn once answered the person twice — Hermes's own auto-resume turn and the companion's redelivered brief — and every per-request expectation still held, because each only asks for a post. The total is where a second answer shows. `error: 2` is the refused question on `desk` (#2235, #2272) and the `onboarding` expiry, an `error` since #2842 (#2925); `cancelled: 1` is the injected stop on `invoices` alone.

🔴 `memoryOps` names `remember` alone (#2386): recall is not counted, because Hermes skips a prefetch on a trivial prompt, so a count would assert Hermes's heuristic; `ledger`'s `expectMemory` step and the runners' `memory_recalled` judgement carry it.
